sources.claim: The SBA lists the launch steps (choose a structure, register, get federal and state tax IDs, apply for licenses and permits, open a business bank account, get insurance) as a general guide.

sections.skill: Explain why business money needs its own account

questions.prompt: What is commingling?

choices.text: Keeping receipts in a folder by month
Paying taxes on time each quarter
Opening several savings accounts at once

questions.intro: A separate business bank account keeps business money apart from personal money. All business income goes in and all business expenses come out of it. This makes bookkeeping and taxes easier, shows clearly what the business earns, and helps support the separation between an LLC or corporation and its owner. Mixing personal and business money in one account is called COMMINGLING. It makes records confusing and can weaken liability protection. The SBA lists opening a business bank account as a launch step.
questions.feedback: Commingling means mixing funds.
